newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Tesco sees margins stabilising.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Tesco sees margins stabilising.

text.p: British supermarket group Tesco Plc on Tuesday expects current low food inflation to continue through to autumn but the 1997-98 year should see inflation steadying and stabilising margins, deputy chairman David Reid told Reuters.
"We think low inflation will probably stay on through until about the autumn," he said in a telephone interview.
"We are anticipating next year to be a stabilising picture on margins...petrol margins are recovering and there seems to be some reasonable stability in food prices currently," he said.
Tesco, which turned in pretax profits up 10 percent to 750 million stg, said current same store sales were up six percent with inflation of one percent.
Gross margins were reduced by 0.4 percent to 5.8 percent and Reid pointed out that 0.3 points of the slip were due to a petrol price war in the first half.
But he said gross margins would be key during the current year.
"Maintaining gross margins will be a key objective" for companies, Reid said.
"I think it will still be very competitive. I think the noise level will still be high...I think you can see that just from the various promotions that are going on," Reid said.
He said Tesco aimed to launch a credit card in early July as a first step in its financial services venture with Royal Bank of Scotland with other products to follow.

Reid said Tesco hoped that its recent purchase of Irish supermarkets from Associated British Foods (ABF) for 630 million stg would see a return on capital on a depreciation basis of around 15 percent compared with around nine percent on the acquisition cost.
He said Tesco's operations in Hungary, where it has bought control of Global T.H., were showing strong sales growth.
"Like for like sales...last year were up 37 percent...so that's why we're there," Reid said.
He said even allowing for inflation of around 19 percent, it was a strong performance."
Tesco plans to open six to eight new stores in Hungary in 1998 along with one in Budapest this year, he said.
Reid said the transition of management, as Lord MacLaurin steps down as chairman later this year, was very smooth and the new team would provide "more of the same."

He said that would include more customer initiatives based on "better prices, improved service, working very hard with ClubCard...further new products and particularly also more money going into refits and extensions."
Tesco aims to open 26 stores in the UK in the current year totalling some 600,000 square feet along with some 200,000 square feet of extensions.
